content: 1. Use an 8-gram suppository as needed for constipation. Retain the suppository for 15 minutes. 2. The patient should lie on their left side with knees bent during administration. 3. Remove the protective wrapper from the suppository before inserting it. 4. Gently insert the tip of the suppository into the rectum using a slight side-to-side motion, ensuring the tip is pointing toward the navel. 5. For liquid suppositories, squeeze the bulb until all the liquid is expelled, then discard the unit. 6. Be aware that excessive bowel activity, cramping pain, rectal irritation, and tenesmus may occur as side effects. 7. Do not use this product in cases of gastrointestinal obstruction or severe fecal impaction. 8. This product is intended for rectal use only. 9. It may cause rectal discomfort, including a burning sensation. 10. Do not use if experiencing abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, or a sudden change in bowel habits lasting more than two weeks, unless directed by a physician. 11. Avoid use if laxatives have already been used for more than one week. 12. Frequent or prolonged use of laxatives may lead to dependency. 13. Discontinue use and seek medical attention if rectal bleeding occurs or if there is no bowel movement after using the product, as these symptoms may require physician care. 14. Do not use this product for longer than one week. 15. Regarding pregnancy, there is no available data on its safety. 16. For lactation, it is not known whether the product is excreted in breast milk, but no risks have been identified for nursing infants. 17. In general, the product is considered acceptable during pregnancy, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
